I do two kinds of consulting.

## measurement & survey design

If your work involves asking people to rate things on a scale — how happy they are, how wrong something is, how much pain they're in — I can help you think about what those numbers actually mean and how to avoid the ways they can mislead you. This is what my research is about, and it turns out the standard practices are worse than most people realize.

I can help with designing better self-report instruments, auditing existing surveys for known measurement artifacts, and understanding when your averages, group comparisons, or effect sizes might be telling you the wrong thing. I'm also available for talks and workshops for research teams.

## writing

I've written for *The New York Times*, *The New Republic*, and *The Daily Beast*, and I've spent a lot of time helping other people get clearer on the page. As a Writing Fellow at Yale's Graduate Writing Lab, I worked with students across disciplines on manuscripts, theses, fellowship applications, and journal submissions. I also run annual NSF GRFP writing workshops for Yale's writing center and personal statement workshops for Yale Sneak Peek.

I'm especially useful if you're trying to translate technical work for a general audience, if you're stuck on a manuscript and need someone to tell you what's actually going wrong, or if you're working on a fellowship or grant application.
